Chapter 192: 0189 The Great Battle is Imminent

*Legends of the Three Kingdoms* and Xiaonei Wang initially used ChinaPay.

The account opening fee was 10,000 yuan, the interface encryption fee was 15,000 yuan, and the annual service fee was around 10,000 yuan, on top of which were transaction fees and a commission.

ChinaPay was certainly secure.

But it was too secure!

Its security controls were incredibly cumbersome and frequently encountered unexpected errors. As a result, the abandonment rate for users who originally wanted to top up was over 30%.

It wasn't until *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* started turning a profit that Chen Guiliang tried to build his own payment system. He continued to use ChinaPay, as there was no conflict.

The English name was YKPay, also called "Youfutong" or "Youfu."

Why not have ByteDance do it?

Because the cost was too high, and it would cause ByteDance's funds to dry up prematurely!

Even The9, when it became the agent for *World of Warcraft* this year, used a third-party payment system called "Huanxun IPS." The9 could certainly afford to burn money, but to seize the gaming market quickly, it didn't dare to build its own payment system and roll it out slowly.

This kind of thing was both time-consuming and expensive.

Game Science also took it one step at a time.

First, they had to spend 1.5 million yuan on a licensing fee to purchase a database. Then they spent another 1 million yuan to buy two IBM minicomputers, which were placed in Peking University's server room for a fee. They hired PKU technical staff to watch over the server room in three shifts, with annual labor costs in the hundreds of thousands.

They also had to form a development team, with annual costs also in the hundreds of thousands. They purchased a risk control system with a one-time payment of 800,000 yuan.

Only with all this in place could they then spend another 1 million yuan to apply for various security certificates.

Next, for each bank they integrated (the big four), they had to pay an access fee and a deposit. ICBC was the most expensive; last year the deposit was 1 million yuan, but it dropped to 800,000 this year. The access fee was 300,000 yuan.

To connect with all four major banks, the deposits and access fees would total over 3 million yuan.

Fortunately, to gain market share, private commercial banks offered free access as long as you took out a 1 million yuan "online banking loan" from them. Accessing several major private banks was free, but it meant carrying several million in high-interest loans.

Up to this point, Game Science's "Youfutong" had only set up online payments.

For the last two or three months, Game Science had been contacting distributors of "prepaid cards." Only after the offline top-up channels for "Youfutong" were established would this payment system be considered somewhat respectable.

And setting up offline top-up channels was something that required grinding it out over time.

Next, they would have to continuously improve the payment system based on actual problems.

It takes at least two to three years for a payment system to mature!

But once it was mature, it would be a goose that lays golden eggs.

Small and medium-sized game developers, as well as some websites, would proactively seek cooperation. Because they had neither the money nor the time to build their own payment systems.

The commission on payments was generally over 30%.

Of course, the operational costs of the payment platform would also increase. Once it grew large enough, it might even have to build its own small server room.

By the way, at this time, building your own payment platform, including Alipay, and acting as a third-party agent for others was a gray area, both legal and not.

The authorities weren't issuing payment licenses, but they also rarely investigated, only occasionally summoning companies for a talk. It was estimated they were letting new things develop to observe the effects.

No matter how good Tao Chenggang's relationship with Chen Guiliang was, he couldn't possibly partner only with Game Science's "Youfutong."

His plan was to cooperate with multiple parties: Youfutong, Yunwang, Junka, Lianbang, and ChinaPay.

Besides top-up services, Youfutong would also provide data for *Reign Under Heaven*, making it easier for Tao Chenggang to adjust the in-game economy.

Yunwang was nominally a third-party payment platform, but in reality, it just sold online prepaid cards. It had a 70% market share.

Junka sold physical prepaid cards in the north.

Lianbang sold physical prepaid cards in the south.

Cooperating with multiple parties could lower the commission charged by distributors. But if pirated prepaid cards appeared, it would be hard to find out which party had leaked them.

"Brother Gang, bad news!"

Yang Yuhui ran up to Tao Chenggang in a hurry, "Zhengtu announced its closed beta will start on the 15th of next month, only one month after ours!"

Tao Chenggang calmly picked up his phone and called Chen Guiliang. "Brother, I need to borrow money. You can take a stake, too."

"How much do you need to borrow?" Chen Guiliang asked.

"1 million," Tao Chenggang said. "My original plan for the closed beta was to slowly release invitation codes to control the number of online players and meticulously save on server costs. But now, it looks like I'll have to increase the number of beta testers ahead of schedule. *Zhengtu*'s closed beta is next month."

Chen Guiliang said, "Let me check and see how much liquid cash Game Science still has."

He couldn't touch ByteDance's money anymore. As the user base for Xiaonei Wang and Kaixin Wang continued to grow, ByteDance's monthly costs were also skyrocketing.

Game Science wasn't exactly rich either, carrying several million in high-interest loans and continuously pouring money into various projects.

A few minutes later, Chen Guiliang said, "I can lend you 1 million, at the bank loan interest rate. If you need to borrow more, I'll have to take the opportunity to invest."

"Thanks!" Tao Chenggang hung up.

For both Tao Chenggang's *Reign Under Heaven* and Boss Shi's *Zhengtu*, the closed beta was not only for finding bugs but also for perfecting the item mall system.

With Chen Guiliang's advice, the item mall system for *Reign Under Heaven* was much more refined than *Zhengtu*'s.

In another timeline, *Zhengtu*'s closed beta with just tens of thousands of players was enough to scare *Legend of Mir* into announcing it was going free-to-play 13 days later. That was because Boss Shi's promotional offensive was too fierce!

But now, with *Reign Under Heaven* jumping in first, who knew how Chen Tianqiao would react.

Chen Guiliang rode his bicycle, leisurely heading back to the dorm.

Today, he had skipped half a day of classes again.

He wasn't the only one becoming more and more brazen; even Jiang Junlai had started to slack off.

This semester, Jiang Junlai had only chosen 17 courses and no longer spent all day in classrooms, study rooms, and the library. He had more time for leisure and entertainment.

It was evening, and Chen Guiliang saw Jiang Junlai and a girl walking back together after eating at the cafeteria.

"Chen Guiliang!"

Jiang Junlai waved enthusiastically.

The girl smiled shyly, "Hello, Student Chen."

"Hello," Chen Guiliang replied.

"Um, I'll head back to my dorm first." The girl left after saying that.

After she was gone, Chen Guiliang asked, "Your girlfriend?"

Jiang Junlai scratched his head. "Not yet, but I do have some feelings for her. Her name is Wen Qiaoqiao. I met her in a class at the School of Physics."

"A girl studying physics?" Chen Guiliang said.

"Yeah," Jiang Junlai said.

Chen Guiliang pushed his bicycle to the front of the dorm building and fastened one lock after another.

Jiang Junlai asked, "After Senior Brother Guo moved dorms, I haven't seen him in a long time. Did he ever win over that goddess of his?"

Chen Guiliang said, "His goddess was accepted into the master's program. That's all I know. But it seems Madman Guo writes the senior sister a letter every week."

"He has her phone number, QQ, and is friends with her on Xiaonei Wang. Why is he writing letters?" Jiang Junlai said, confused.

"How should I know? Maybe he thinks it's more romantic," Chen Guiliang said.

The two returned to dorm room 404, where their two freshman roommates were sitting in front of Chen Guiliang's computer.

His computer had practically become a public one.

"What are you guys arguing about?" Jiang Junlai tossed his books on the table.

Li Heng said, "Choosing the campus belle! Xiaonei Wang has already decided that the second week of October every year will be the National Campus Belle Election Week."

New students start in September, and after mixing in for over a month, they're basically familiar with everyone. It was the most suitable time to vote for the campus belle.

An annual event.

"Ah, I totally forgot about this!"

Jiang Junlai squeezed over. "Move aside, I need to vote for the beauties."

Tong Zhihong moved out of the way, his tone quite regretful. "There haven't been any great beauties in our Yuanpei Program for the past few years, so I don't know who to choose as our department belle. Alas, I can only vote for girls from other schools and departments for the campus belle."

Chen Guiliang lay on his bed and sent a text to Bian Guanyue: "Student Campus Belle Bian, are you going to win again this year?"

"Hee hee, maybe."

"Have any guys been pursuing you?"

"After you made that scene last year, and now that everyone knows who you are, even if guys like me, they only dare to find excuses to get close. They're afraid of being rejected if they pursue me directly."

"Then you should thank me for scaring off those troublesome guys for you."

"Hmph! I uploaded another song, recorded during the National Day holiday."

"I've listened to it. I have a suggestion. Don't you know Sichuan opera? You could totally learn from Jay Chou and write Chinese-style songs like 'East Wind Breaks.'"

"Chinese style is still based on Western melodies; it has nothing to do with traditional opera. They're two completely different systems."

"I meant adding a few lines of operatic-style singing."
